top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an original invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms), distinct from the comb and ion-control prizes, verified by independent laboratories at the 10^-18 level, and it opens a door to gravitational redshift, constants and dark-matter tests. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye is clean and the citation is scoped to the magic-wavelength lattice clock; the remaining priority questions (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Oates) are real but do not justify withholding the prize.
recusal_note: Fellow of the University of Tokyo (Katori's institution) since 2025 and long-running exchanges with the Tokyo microscopy community; a general institutional link, not a personal or collaborative one, so no recusal appears required.
